h1: Residency Scheduling Software? We Can Build the Schedule For You
paragraph: Go beyond typical residency scheduling software. Scheduling Wizard is a managed service. Provide your rules; we deliver a complete schedule built to the ACGME requirements.

cta.title: Get Your Residency Schedules Done Right
cta.description: Book a call to talk through your scheduling needs and learn how Scheduling Wizard works. Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that have us build their call, block, clinic and shift schedules.

faq.answer: Residency scheduling software helps programs build and manage rotation, call, and clinic schedules for residents. Most tools are self-service platforms that require someone to learn and operate them. Scheduling Wizard is different: it is a managed service, not a self-service platform. Programs submit their rules and receive finished schedules, built to your rules, as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you. There is no software to learn, no dashboard to manage, and no annual retraining needed when chief residents rotate.
faq.question: What is residency scheduling software and how does Scheduling Wizard differ?

faq.answer: ACGME compliance is built into the schedule as it is created, not manually checked after the fact. The subspecialty requirements you tell us apply are built in, including the 80-hour limit (averaged over four weeks), minimum rest requirements, and program-specific call rules. Because the rules are built in as the schedule is created, the rules are applied before the schedule reaches your program. It is the first thing most programs ask, and the answer is the same: you tell us which requirements apply, we write them down with you, and we build to them.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle the ACGME duty hour rules?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard generates four types of schedules: Block or rotation schedules, Call schedules with fair call distribution, Clinic schedules, and Attending schedules. All four are built together, so conflicts between schedule types are resolved before the final schedule is delivered. The output is delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you, ready for your existing publishing platform.
faq.question: What types of schedules does Scheduling Wizard generate for residency programs?

faq.answer: No. It is entirely up to you. We build the schedule either way, and deliver it in the format and structure you want: Excel or Google Sheets, or a custom live view we build for you if that is useful. Many programs keep the platform they already have for day-to-day viewing and upload our schedules straight into it; others use the live view, or both. Whatever works best for your program.
faq.question: Do we need to replace the platform we use now to use Scheduling Wizard?

faq.answer: Your program's rules and requests are written down and kept year over year. When a new chief resident takes over, they inherit the written rule set and last year's schedule. This removes one of the most common sources of scheduling disruption in residency programs, where institutional knowledge is lost every time a chief resident rotates out.
faq.question: What happens to our scheduling setup when chief residents change each year?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard works with chief residents, program directors, program coordinators, and GME offices. Chief residents are often the primary point of contact since they are typically responsible for building schedules. Program directors and coordinators are also common contacts, particularly for larger programs or those managing schedules across multiple departments. The managed service model is designed so that no single person needs deep scheduling expertise to get compliant, finished schedules produced.
